newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up at 35.865/875 against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up at 35.865/875 against dollar.

text.p: The rupee closed Tuesday at 35.865/875 against the dollar, up from 35.89/90 opening, dealers said on Tuesday.
"Everyone was waiting for the dollar to rally today," said the chief forex dealer at an Indian bank. "Actually the rupee rallied."
The spot market continued almost steady at 35.88/89 until noon when a leading company sold dollars, dealers said.
Banks which began the day in the hope of a dollar rally ahead of Friday's budget presentation had to contend with a rupee which hardened to 35.86/87 against the dollar.
The Reserve Bank of India was in the market to buy dollars at 35.8750 level towards the end of the day's trading.
"The market was right (in predicting) that the rupee would be stable until the budget," said a dealer.
"But no one knows what's to happen after the budget."
The rupee's periodic revivals at a time when most dealers are looking forward to a faster depreciation has been a chastening experience to most dealers.
Some dealers wondered why Indian exporters are not complaining about the overvalued rupee.
The forward dollar market saw the premia continuing to climb, braked by occasional bouts of profit-booking.
The six month annualised premium closed Tuesday at 7.47 percent, unchanged from the previous close, dealers said.
"But the trend (for premia) is up," said a dealer.
